senses.gloss: m. (נָקַשׁ) [clapping together,] comparing, correspondence; esp. hekkesh, the analogy between two laws which rests on a biblical intimation (as Lev. XIV, 13) or on a principle common to both.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 6:1:2">Y. Pes. VI, beg., 33ᵃ</cite> <he>מה׳ הואיל ותמיד וכ׳</he> he derived the law that the Passover sacrifice supersedes the Sabbath (v. <cite ref="D00397"><he>דָּחָה</he></cite>) by drawing an analogy: as the daily offering is &c., (contrad. to <he>גזירה שוה</he>, v. <cite ref="C00581"><he>גְּזֵרָה</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Zevachim 49b:14">Zeb. 49ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>דבר הלמד בה׳ חוזר וכ׳</he> a law which is derived by analogy may be used for deriving another law by analogy; a. fr.
